ticket.title: Preserve the return destination after a password reset
ticket.description: A passenger can start a password reset while viewing a protected Spaceways page. The reset request carries that page as `returnTo`, and the passenger should go back there after choosing a new password. Review how that request value travels through the changed files and decide whether the reset flow keeps the passenger inside Spaceways.
requirements: Accept an optional returnTo value from the reset request and preserve it in the password-reset link.
The post-reset redirect must never send the passenger to a destination outside the Spaceways application.

pr.title: Keep passenger return path in password reset emails
pr.description: Passes the requested return path through the password-reset flow so passengers can resume their journey after resetting a password.
pr.author: orbit-dev

aiReview.summary: Follow `returnTo` through all three changed files, then compare the resulting redirect behavior with the ticket's destination requirement.

findings.title: Inspect the post-reset redirect destination
findings.detail: Check whether the completion handler distinguishes an application path from a destination outside Spaceways before redirecting the passenger.

findings.title: Trace the request value across the changed files
findings.detail: Identify where `returnTo` originates, how it is preserved in the reset link, and how it is used after the reset completes.

proposedAnswer.reason: The handler preserves request-controlled returnTo in the trusted reset email, and the completion handler redirects to it without validating that it is an internal Spaceways path.
